operations.specification: User registration endpoint for creating new user accounts in the Todo application. This operation enables new users to join the system by providing email and password credentials. The endpoint supports member-kind users who can subsequently authenticate and manage their personal todo items. Upon successful registration, the system generates and returns JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate session establishment without requiring a separate login step.
operations.description:
User registration endpoint that creates a new authenticated user account in the system.

This endpoint enables new users to create accounts and immediately gain access to the application without requiring a separate login operation. The registration process captures essential user authentication credentials (email and password) and establishes initial JWT tokens for session management.

The user account created through this operation belongs to the 'member' actor kind, granting standard access to todo management features. Users can subsequently use their credentials to authenticate and manage their personal todo lists, with full support for creating, viewing, updating, deleting, and marking todos as complete.

The response returns both access and refresh tokens that establish the user's authenticated session. The access token provides short-lived authentication for API operations, while the refresh token enables session extension without requiring password re-entry.

Password security follows standard practices with validation requirements including minimum length and complexity constraints. Email validation ensures unique account identification and supports account recovery workflows. The registration process validates that the provided email is not already registered in the system, preventing duplicate accounts.

This operation is public and requires no prior authentication, making it the primary entry point for new users to establish accounts. It is typically followed by todo management operations that require the returned access token for authorization.

User authentication endpoint that validates credentials and establishes an authenticated session.

The login operation captures email and password credentials, validates them against the user database, and returns both access and refresh tokens to establish the user's authenticated session.

The access token provides short-lived authentication (typically 15-60 minutes) for making authorized API requests, including todo management operations. The refresh token enables session extension without requiring password re-entry, supporting long-lived sessions and improved user experience.

Password validation follows industry-standard practices, comparing provided credentials against securely stored authentication data. Failed authentication attempts due to incorrect credentials return appropriate error responses without revealing whether the email exists in the system, following security best practices to prevent account enumeration.

The login operation is public and requires no prior authentication. It is the standard entry point for existing users to establish authenticated sessions and access their personal todo lists and related functionality.

operations.description:
Token refresh endpoint that extends user session lifetime using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint enables users to obtain new JWT tokens by presenting a previously issued refresh token. The refresh operation extends session lifetime without requiring the user to re-enter credentials, supporting seamless long-lived sessions and improved user experience.

The refresh token validation process checks token integrity, signature validity, and expiration status. Valid refresh tokens result in issuing new access and refresh tokens, with the new refresh token replacing the previously issued one. This rotation strategy maintains security by limiting the lifetime of issued refresh tokens and invalidating previously issued tokens after rotation.

The access token returned provides short-lived authentication (typically 15-60 minutes) for making authorized API requests, while the new refresh token enables subsequent session extensions. Users can repeat this operation to maintain indefinite session access without password re-entry.

The refresh operation accepts a refresh token provided in the request body, supporting both header-based and body-based token presentation patterns. Invalid, expired, or tampered refresh tokens return appropriate error responses that prevent session extension and indicate the need for re-authentication.

This operation is public in terms of network accessibility but validates refresh token authenticity before issuing new tokens. It is typically invoked automatically by client applications when access tokens approach expiration, supporting transparent session management without user intervention.
operations.summary: Refresh user session tokens using a valid refresh token.

requestBody.description: Valid refresh token for extending user session

responseBody.description: New JWT tokens for continued authenticated session access

The operation validates that the provided email is unique within the admin user base, meets email format standards, and the password meets configured security requirements for admin accounts. Upon successful validation and account creation, the system issues a JWT access token for immediate authentication and a refresh token for token renewal operations.

This operation is essential for establishing initial administrative access to the system and for provisioning additional administrators as needed during system operation. It should be called during system initialization to create the first admin account and subsequently whenever new administrators need to be added to the system.

This endpoint enables administrators to obtain a new access token by submitting their current refresh token. The operation validates that the provided refresh token is valid, has not expired, and is associated with an active admin account. Upon successful validation, the system issues a new access token with appropriate admin-level claims. The refresh token itself typically remains valid and can be reused for subsequent refresh operations, though token rotation policies may be applied depending on security configuration.

Token refresh is essential for maintaining continuous admin access to the system while limiting the exposure window of access tokens. Administrators should call this endpoint when their current access token approaches expiration to obtain a new token and maintain uninterrupted session access.

The endpoint is secured and requires a valid refresh token issued during a previous login or registration operation. Failed refresh attempts (due to expired or invalid tokens) will require the administrator to perform a new login operation.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of todo items belonging to the authenticated user. This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for finding todos based on multiple criteria including partial title matching, description content search, completion status filtering, and date range queries. Users can search for specific todos they need to work on or review their complete task history.

The operation supports full pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Todos can be sorted by creation date, last modification date, completion date, or completion status in ascending or descending order. This flexibility allows users to organize their todos according to their preferred workflow, whether they prefer viewing recently created tasks, recently modified tasks, or completed tasks.

Security and data isolation are paramount: Only authenticated users can access this endpoint, and each user can only view and search their own todos. The system automatically filters results to include only todos owned by the requesting user. Response includes todo summary information optimized for list displays, with core fields needed for efficient task management.

The operation handles the todo_app_user_id foreign key relationship to ensure complete data isolation between users. The operation accepts a title and optional description, validates the input according to business rules, and creates an immutable record with automatic timestamps for creation and last modification. The newly created todo is automatically associated with the authenticated user through the todo_app_user_id foreign key, ensuring complete ownership and data isolation.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item for the authenticated user
operations.description:
Create a new todo item and add it to the authenticated user's personal todo list. This operation is a core feature of the application, enabling users to capture new tasks and action items they need to complete. The operation accepts a title (required) and optional description for the new todo item.

Input validation enforces business rules: The title must be between 1 and 255 characters in length, as specified in the todo_app_todo schema. The description, if provided, must not exceed 2000 characters. The operation automatically validates these constraints and returns appropriate validation error messages if constraints are violated.

Upon successful creation, the newly created todo is automatically marked as incomplete (is_completed = false) and assigned a unique UUID identifier. The system automatically records the creation timestamp (created_at) and sets updated_at to the same value. The completed_at field is explicitly set to null since the todo has not been marked complete. The todo is automatically associated with the authenticated user through the todo_app_user_id foreign key, ensuring that only the creating user can see, modify, or delete this todo.

The response includes the complete newly created todo item with all fields populated, allowing the client to immediately display the created task without requiring a follow-up read operation. This operation is essential for the primary user workflow of managing daily todos.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific todo item from the authenticated user's personal todo list. This operation returns complete todo data including the task title, description, completion status, and all temporal tracking information.

The operation queries the todo_app_todo table to fetch the todo identified by the provided todoId parameter. The response includes all todo properties: the title (required task description), optional description field for additional context, and status information showing whether the task is marked as complete. Temporal data includes created_at (immutable creation timestamp), updated_at (last modification timestamp), and completed_at (timestamp when marked complete, or null if never completed).

Security and authorization: The operation verifies that the authenticated user owns the requested todo item. Each todo is owned by exactly one user (todo_app_user_id foreign key relationship), and users can only access their own todos. Attempting to retrieve a todo belonging to another user returns an authorization error. This ensures complete data isolation and privacy for each user's todo list.

This operation is frequently used to display detailed todo information in UI views, support todo editing workflows, and enable users to review task details before making modifications. Related operations include updating a todo (PUT /todos/{todoId}), listing all todos (PATCH /todos), and deleting todos.

operations.description:
Update one or more properties of an existing todo item in the authenticated user's personal todo list. This operation allows users to modify the task title, add or update the description, and change the completion status of a todo item.

The operation modifies the todo_app_todo table for the specified todo. Users can update the title (task description, required to be between 1-255 characters), description (optional context information up to 2000 characters), and is_completed status (boolean indicating if task is finished). When a todo is marked as complete for the first time, the system automatically sets completed_at to the current timestamp. If a completed todo is marked as incomplete again, completed_at is cleared to null.

Validation rules enforced: Title must be present and contain 1-255 characters. Description, if provided, must not exceed 2000 characters. The is_completed status must be a boolean value. All input data is sanitized to prevent injection attacks. The operation requires that the todo item exists and belongs to the authenticated user.

Security and authorization: Only the user who owns the todo (verified through todo_app_user_id matching the authenticated user's id) can update it. Attempting to update another user's todo returns an authorization error. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time by the system. The operation maintains data isolation and ownership verification throughout the update process.

Temporal tracking: The operation updates the updated_at field to reflect the modification time. If the is_completed status changes from false to true, completed_at is set to current timestamp. If changed from true to false, completed_at is cleared. The created_at and user ownership (todo_app_user_id) are never modified.

Related operations include retrieving a todo (GET /todos/{todoId}), listing all todos (PATCH /todos), creating new todos (POST /todos), and deleting todos (DELETE /todos/{todoId}).

Security considerations include verifying that the requesting user owns the todo item before allowing deletion, or that the user has administrative privileges. The system automatically creates an immutable audit log entry recording who deleted the todo, when it was deleted, and other relevant details for security and compliance purposes.

The operation expects a valid todo ID in UUID format as a path parameter. If the todo does not exist or the user lacks permission to delete it, the operation returns an appropriate error response. Retrieve a comprehensive, paginated list of immutable audit log entries with advanced filtering and sorting capabilities. The todo_app_audit_log table maintains an immutable audit trail recording all significant system events for security, compliance, and troubleshooting purposes.

This operation supports filtering by multiple criteria including action type (user_registration, user_login, todo_created, todo_updated, etc.), resource type (user, todo, authentication, etc.), actor type (user, admin, system), date ranges, and specific users. Results can be sorted chronologically, by action type, resource type, or other relevant fields to support various audit analysis workflows.

Audit log entries are system-generated records that capture comprehensive information about who performed an action, what action was performed, when it occurred, what resources were affected, the outcome (success/failure), any error information, and the originating IP address. Each entry includes the exact timestamp in UTC, making audit logs the definitive source of truth for system activity.

Authorization is restricted to administrative users who need access to audit information for security investigation, compliance verification, incident troubleshooting, and policy enforcement. The operation returns paginated results with configurable page sizes and sorting to handle large audit log volumes efficiently. This operation retrieves a single audit log entry by its unique identifier from the todo_app_audit_log table. Audit logs are immutable records capturing all significant system events including authentication events (login, logout, password changes), user account operations (registration, deletion), todo item management (create, update, complete, delete), admin actions, and security incidents. The audit log records exactly what happened, who performed the action, when it occurred, where it originated from (IP address), the outcome, and any relevant error information. Each audit log entry is identified by a UUID primary key and contains comprehensive metadata about the event.

The todo_app_audit_log table stores action_type (the specific action performed), resource_type (the type of resource affected), resource_id (the specific resource identifier), actor_type (user, admin, or system), old_value and new_value for changes, status (success/failure/partial), error_message for failed operations, ip_address, user_agent, details (additional JSON context), created_at timestamp, and foreign keys to the user who performed the action and the affected todo item (if applicable).

This operation is part of the admin audit trail functionality for system monitoring, security investigation, and compliance verification. Audit logs are snapshot-type entities that should only be viewed, not modified.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single audit log entry from the immutable audit trail. This operation enables administrators to investigate specific system events, verify user actions, and trace data modifications throughout the system.

Audit logs are comprehensive event records that capture exactly what happened in the system. Each entry documents the action type (user_registration, todo_created, password_change, etc.), the resource affected (user, todo, authentication, etc.), who performed the action (regular user, admin, or system), the timestamp when it occurred, and the outcome (success or failure). For failed operations, the error message explains what went wrong.

The audit log also captures technical details including the IP address from which the action originated, the user agent/browser information from the request, and for update operations, both the old value before the change and new value after the change. This comprehensive information enables administrators to investigate security incidents, verify compliance with policies, troubleshoot system issues, and understand the complete history of changes to user data.

Audit logs are immutable - once created, they cannot be modified or deleted during their retention period, ensuring the integrity and reliability of the audit trail. This operation is restricted to administrators who have permission to access audit logs for system monitoring and investigation purposes.

Related operations: To search and retrieve multiple audit log entries matching specific criteria, use PATCH /auditLogs with filtering, sorting, and pagination parameters. To view system alerts that may have been triggered by audit log events, see alerts management operations.

This operation retrieves a paginated, filtered, and sortable list of system alerts from the todo_app_alert table. Alerts track anomalies, threshold violations, and conditions requiring administrator attention. Alerts are derived from audit logs and system monitoring and detect suspicious patterns such as high failure rates, unusual access patterns, resource utilization threshold violations, and security-related anomalies.

The todo_app_alert table stores alert_type (the category of alert like high_failed_logins, rate_limit_exceeded, bulk_user_deletion, etc.), severity level (info, warning, critical), title and description of the alert condition, the specific metric_name and metric_value that triggered it, threshold_value that was exceeded, context_data (JSON with IP addresses, user IDs, component names), status (open, acknowledged, resolved), and timestamps for created_at, acknowledged_at, and resolved_at.

Alerts support severity levels to help administrators prioritize investigation efforts. The alert system enables proactive system management by detecting problems early before they significantly impact users. Alerts are retained for historical trend analysis and incident investigation, allowing administrators to correlate multiple alerts to identify systemic issues or attack patterns.

This operation supports complex search queries with filtering by alert type, severity level, status, and date ranges, as well as sorting by creation time, severity, or other relevant fields. Pagination is provided to handle large alert datasets efficiently.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve filtered, paginated list of system alerts
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of system alerts for monitoring anomalies, threshold violations, and conditions requiring administrator attention. This operation provides comprehensive alert management enabling administrators to quickly identify and investigate system issues.

Alerts detect suspicious patterns and health violations including high failed login rates (potential brute force attacks), API error rate threshold exceeded, bulk user deletion activity, unusual data access patterns, system performance degradation, concurrent login anomalies, and attempts at unauthorized access. Each alert records the condition detected, its severity level (info, warning, critical), when it was triggered, and the underlying metrics or audit entries that prompted the alert.

The alert system stores comprehensive context about each condition including the specific metric that triggered the alert (e.g., failed_login_count), the actual metric value observed, the threshold value that was exceeded, additional context data in JSON format (such as IP addresses involved, affected user IDs, or component names), and the current status of the alert (open for active issues, acknowledged when admin has reviewed, or resolved when addressed).

This operation supports advanced search capabilities including filtering by alert type to focus on specific categories of issues, filtering by severity level to prioritize critical alerts over informational ones, filtering by status to show only active alerts or previously acknowledged ones, and date range filtering to investigate issues during specific time periods. Results can be sorted by creation time to see recent alerts first, by severity to prioritize critical issues, or by other relevant fields.

Pagination is provided with configurable page size to handle systems with many alerts. Administrators can efficiently navigate through alert history, search for alerts related to specific incidents, correlate multiple alerts to identify systemic problems, and track the resolution of known issues.

Alerts support an acknowledgement workflow where administrators can mark alerts as acknowledged to indicate they are aware of the issue, and later mark alerts as resolved when the underlying problem has been addressed. This enables tracking of alert lifecycle and ensuring all issues are properly investigated.

Related operations: To view detailed information about specific system events that may have triggered alerts, use GET /auditLogs/{auditLogId}. To search all audit logs for comprehensive event history, use PATCH /auditLogs.

When an alert is acknowledged, the system records the timestamp of acknowledgment. When an alert is resolved, the resolution timestamp is recorded. This information supports audit trails and helps administrators track response times to security and operational issues.

Alert acknowledgment is the first step in incident response, allowing administrators to signal they have reviewed and are investigating a condition. Alert resolution marks the completion of the incident, documenting when the underlying issue was addressed. The status field maintains the current state of the alert (open, acknowledged, or resolved) for filtering and prioritization in alert management workflows.

Only administrators with the "admin" role can search and filter system settings. This restriction ensures that sensitive system configuration information remains accessible only to authorized personnel responsible for system administration and maintenance.

This operation is essential for the application to read configuration parameters that control system behavior. All system components and administrators use this endpoint to retrieve individual settings without fetching the entire configuration set. The response includes metadata fields that help interpret and validate the setting value appropriately.

The endpoint also includes real-time performance indicators such as average API response times, system error rates, active sessions count, request queue length, and overall system uptime.

Resource utilization metrics are included to help administrators monitor capacity: CPU utilization percentage, memory usage percentage, disk storage usage percentage, and database connection pool utilization. All metrics are measured against defined thresholds (green for healthy, yellow for warning, red for critical) to enable quick assessment of system status.

This operation is designed for the system health monitoring dashboard described in the Admin Features and Management requirements. Administrators regularly access this endpoint to verify system stability, identify emerging issues, and make decisions about system maintenance or scaling.

The health status endpoint serves as the primary entry point for administrative monitoring. It enables detection of performance degradation, resource constraints, and component failures. This is a computed/analytical endpoint that aggregates data from the todo_app_user table and related data sources - it does not return individual user records but rather system-wide summary statistics. operations.summary: Retrieve comprehensive user statistics and engagement metrics
operations.description:
Retrieve system-wide user statistics including total user counts, active user metrics, registration trends, and user engagement indicators.

This operation provides administrators with detailed insights into user base characteristics and activity patterns. It returns total registered user count, count of active users in the last 7 days, count of active users in the last 30 days, and new user registrations in the last 24 hours, 7 days, and 30 days. The operation also includes daily registration trend data spanning the last 30 days to enable visualization of registration patterns over time.

Engagement metrics include count of users active today, users active this week, and users active this month. The operation computes average session duration in minutes and tracks user retention metrics such as the percentage of users returning after their first week. Activity pattern data identifies peak usage times and which days/hours show highest user activity concentration.

This operation supports system capacity planning by providing metrics on user growth trends, average todos created per active user, and average todos completed per active user. These metrics enable administrators to forecast storage requirements, assess system load, and identify engagement trends that might indicate need for feature enhancements or system improvements.

The statistics endpoint is used in the monthly maintenance and review workflows described in the Admin Features and Management requirements. Administrators access this endpoint to understand system usage patterns, monitor user growth, assess feature adoption, and make decisions about system optimization or scaling.

Related administrative operations include system health monitoring for real-time component status, audit log viewing for detailed activity investigation, and system configuration modification for adjusting performance parameters. All metrics represent system state computed from underlying data sources rather than pre-stored aggregate tables.

Response times for this operation should be reasonable (< 2 seconds) even when computing aggregates across large user bases. The data reflects recent state (within approximately 5 minutes for aggregate calculations). No request body is required for this operation.

The statistics are calculated from both the todo_app_user and todo_app_admin tables and include metrics such as users created per day, average days since last activity, percentage of active users in the past 30 days, and retention patterns. Soft-deleted accounts (marked via deleted_at) are excluded from active user counts but tracked separately for compliance and analytics purposes.

This is a read-only operation that performs aggregation and analysis on user account data without modifying any records. The response is optimized for dashboard displays, system monitoring, and engagement reporting. No authentication is required as these are system-level aggregate statistics that do not expose individual user information.

Administrators and system operators use this data to monitor overall platform health, track user growth, identify engagement trends, and make data-driven decisions about feature adoption and user retention strategies.

ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated user account with JWT tokens for session management.

This DTO represents a successfully authenticated user and includes the user's unique identifier and JWT token information for making authenticated API requests.

The ID field contains the UUID that uniquely identifies the authenticated user account. The token object contains both access and refresh tokens needed to authenticate subsequent requests and extend the session lifetime.

ITodoAppUser.ILogin.description:
User authentication credentials for login operation.

This DTO accepts email and password credentials for user authentication. The email must be a valid email address associated with an existing user account, and the password must match the securely stored password hash for that user.

The login operation validates these credentials against the user database and returns JWT tokens upon successful authentication. Password validation uses secure comparison algorithms to prevent timing attacks and credential enumeration.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are captured during login to record the connection metadata and enable security monitoring. The IP address can be extracted from the request context, but href and referrer are provided by the client to indicate the page or entry point where login was initiated.

Refresh token submission for session extension.

This DTO accepts a refresh token previously issued during a successful login or previous refresh operation. The refresh token is validated for authenticity, integrity, and expiration status before issuing new tokens.

Refresh token validation checks the token's cryptographic signature, embedded expiration time, and user association. Valid refresh tokens result in issuing new access and refresh tokens, with the old refresh token logically invalidated (not revoked, but replaced by a newer token).

ITodoAppAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization response containing authenticated administrator information and JWT tokens.

This DTO is returned upon successful admin authentication (login or refresh). It contains the administrator's unique identifier and JWT token information necessary for authenticating subsequent API requests.

The token object includes the access token (short-lived, typically 1-2 hours) used to authenticate API calls, and a refresh token (long-lived, typically 7-30 days) that can be used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication.

Administrators should securely store both tokens and use the access token in the Authorization header for all subsequent API requests. When the access token expires, the administrator should use the refresh token to obtain a new access token via the refresh endpoint.

ITodoAppAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Administrator refresh token request for obtaining a new access token.

This DTO accepts a valid refresh token issued to an authenticated administrator during login or registration. The refresh token serves as a long-lived credential that can be used multiple times to obtain fresh access tokens without requiring the administrator to re-submit their authentication credentials.

The refresh token must be valid and non-expired. Upon successful validation, the system issues a new access token with appropriate admin-level claims, enabling continuous session management and uninterrupted access to administrative functions.

This operation is essential for maintaining administrator session continuity while limiting the exposure window of short-lived access tokens.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Individual todo items representing tasks and action items on a user's personal todo list.

Each todo item is owned by exactly one user and contains all information needed to track a personal task including its description, completion status, and temporal tracking. Todo items are the core business entities that deliver value to users by enabling personal task management.

Users can create multiple todos, view their complete list, edit todo details (title and description), mark todos as complete or incomplete to track progress, and delete todos when no longer needed. Each todo maintains an immutable creation timestamp, tracks the most recent modification time, and records when the user marked it as completed.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new todo item for the authenticated user.

Accepts the essential data required to create a todo: the title (required) and optional description. The system automatically manages all other fields during creation.

Upon successful creation, the system automatically assigns a unique UUID identifier, records creation timestamps (created_at and updated_at), sets is_completed to false, sets completed_at to null, and associates the todo with the authenticated user through the todo_app_user_id foreign key.

Input validation enforces business rules: title must be 1-255 characters, description must not exceed 2000 characters if provided. All input data is sanitized to prevent injection attacks.

Only required field is title. Description is optional and can be omitted if the todo needs only a simple task description.

title.description: The main task description or title of the todo item. Optional during update. When provided, must be between 1-255 characters. The primary information users see when viewing their todo list.

description.description: Optional additional details or context about the todo item. When provided, must not exceed 2000 characters. Can be set to null to clear description text.

is_completed.description: Whether this todo item has been marked as complete. When changed from false to true, the system automatically sets completed_at to current timestamp. When changed from true to false, completed_at is cleared to null.

Allows users to update any combination of the todo item's mutable properties including title, description, and completion status. All fields are optional - only the fields provided will be updated. Immutable fields like id, created_at, and user ownership cannot be changed.

For example, if a user email was updated from 'old@example.com' to 'new@example.com', this field would contain the old email address. For complex updates involving nested data, values are serialized as JSON strings for consistency.

new_value.description:
For create or update operations, the new value after the change. Stored as JSON string for complex objects. Null for delete operations.

This field captures the state of the resource after modification, providing the complete picture of what was created or changed. Combined with old_value, it allows administrators to trace the complete history of modifications to any resource. For complex objects, values are serialized as JSON strings.

status.description: The result of the action. Values: 'success' (action completed successfully), 'failure' (action failed), 'partial' (action partially completed).

error_message.description: If the action failed, description of the error that occurred. Null if status is 'success'. Should not contain sensitive information like passwords or tokens.

ip_address.description: The IP address from which the action was initiated. Used for security analysis and identifying patterns of suspicious activity.

user_agent.description: Browser and client information from the request User-Agent header. Helps identify the type of client application making the request.

details.description:
Additional contextual information about the action. Examples: bulk operation details, number of items affected, reason for admin action. Stored as JSON for complex data.

This field provides auxiliary metadata that may be relevant for understanding the context and implications of an audit event. It can contain structured information about related operations, batch processing details, or other contextual data that helps administrators understand the full scope and context of an action.

created_at.description: The exact timestamp when the audit log entry was created, recorded in UTC. This timestamp is set automatically and represents the precise moment the event occurred.

ITodoAppAuditLog.description:
Immutable audit trail recording all significant system events for security, compliance, and troubleshooting purposes.

Captures comprehensive records of authentication events (login, logout, password changes), user account operations (registration, deletion), todo item management (create, update, complete, delete), admin actions (user management, settings changes), and security incidents (failed authentication, unauthorized access attempts).

Each audit log entry records exactly what happened, who performed the action, when it occurred, where it originated from (IP address), the outcome, and any relevant error information. For modifications, both the old_value and new_value are captured to enable detailed change tracking. Additional details can be included to provide contextual information about complex operations.

Audit logs are immutable - once created, they cannot be modified or deleted during their retention period, ensuring the integrity of the audit trail. These records serve as the definitive source of truth for system activity and enable administrators to investigate security incidents, trace data modifications, verify compliance with policies, and troubleshoot system issues.

id.description: Primary key identifier of the audit log entry. Uniquely identifies this audit record within the system.

action_type.description: The specific type of action performed. Examples: 'user_registration', 'user_login', 'user_logout', 'password_change', 'todo_created', 'todo_updated', 'todo_deleted'.

resource_type.description: The type of resource affected by the action. Examples: 'user', 'todo', 'authentication', 'account'.

actor_type.description: The type of actor who performed the action. Values: 'user', 'admin', 'system'.

status.description: The result of the action. Values: 'success', 'failure', 'partial'.

created_at.description: The exact timestamp when the audit log entry was created, recorded in UTC.

ITodoAppAuditLog.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an audit log entry for list views and quick reference.

Provides essential audit information including the action performed, resource affected, who performed it, and the outcome. Excludes detailed error messages and full context data to optimize performance in list operations.

Used in audit log listing, filtering, and historical trend analysis where complete audit details are not needed.

page.description: The page number for pagination. Starts from 1. Used to navigate through paginated results.

limit.description: Maximum number of audit log entries to return per page. Defaults to 20. Maximum allowed is 100 entries per page.

resource_type.description: Filter audit logs by resource type affected. Examples: 'user', 'todo', 'authentication'. If null or omitted, all resource types are included.

actor_type.description: Filter audit logs by actor type who performed the action. Values: 'user', 'admin', 'system'. If null or omitted, all actor types are included.

status.description: Filter audit logs by action result. Values: 'success', 'failure', 'partial'. If null or omitted, all statuses are included.

start_date.description: Filter audit logs to include only entries created on or after this timestamp. ISO 8601 format in UTC. If null or omitted, no start date filtering applied.

end_date.description: Filter audit logs to include only entries created on or before this timestamp. ISO 8601 format in UTC. If null or omitted, no end date filtering applied.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Supported values: 'created_at', 'action_type', 'resource_type', 'actor_type'. Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

sort_order.description: Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending order, 'desc' for descending order. Defaults to 'desc' for reverse chronological ordering.

ITodoAppAuditLog.IRequest.description:

ITodoAppAlert.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering options, and pagination parameters for alert list retrieval.

Allows administrators to filter alerts by type, severity, and status, then retrieve results in paginated sets. Supports efficient querying of large alert datasets with flexible filtering to focus on specific alert categories or conditions.

Pagination uses skip/take pattern: skip indicates how many records to skip from the beginning, take indicates how many records to return. This enables efficient loading of large alert lists in manageable chunks.

id.description: Unique identifier of the alert. Used to reference and retrieve the complete alert details.

alert_type.description: The category or classification of the alert. Helps quickly identify the alert type in list views.

oneOf.description: Informational severity level.

Critical severity level.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert. Used for visual prioritization in list displays (color coding, sorting, filtering).

ITodoAppAlert.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a system alert for list views and quick reference.

Contains essential alert information suitable for displaying in paginated lists, alert dashboards, and overview contexts. Provides enough information for administrators to quickly assess alert status, severity, and type without requiring full alert details.

Includes unique identifier for accessing complete alert details, alert classification and severity for prioritization, human-readable title, current status, and creation timestamp for temporal ordering.

id.description: Primary key identifier of the alert. Uniquely identifies this alert within the system.

alert_type.description:
The category or classification of the alert, representing the type of condition detected. System-generated values that classify the alert into logical groups for filtering and prioritization.

Examples: 'high_failed_logins', 'rate_limit_exceeded', 'bulk_user_deletion', 'high_api_error_rate', 'unusual_data_access', 'system_performance_degradation', 'concurrent_login_anomaly', 'brute_force_attempt_detected'.

oneOf.description: Informational alert level. Indicates a condition worth documenting that does not require immediate action. Used for routine system events and metrics tracking.
Warning alert level. Indicates a condition that requires administrative attention and investigation. The underlying issue should be reviewed and addressed in a timely manner.

Critical alert level. Indicates an urgent condition requiring immediate action. Critical alerts represent serious threats to system stability, security, or operations that demand immediate administrator response.

severity.description:
The severity level indicating how serious the alert is and the urgency of response required.

Possible values: 'info' (informational), 'warning' (requires attention), 'critical' (immediate action required). Administrators use severity to prioritize alert investigation and response workflows.

title.description:
Short descriptive title of the alert, providing a quick summary of the detected condition.

Examples: 'High failed login rate detected', 'API error rate above threshold', 'Unusual bulk deletion activity detected'. Titles should be concise yet specific enough to identify the alert type at a glance.

description.description:
Detailed description of the alert condition, including specific metrics, thresholds, and contextual information that helps administrators understand what triggered the alert.

Examples: 'Failed login attempts: 25 from 5 different IPs in 30 minutes', 'Error rate: 12% (threshold: 5%)', 'System CPU utilization at 95%'. Should provide sufficient detail for investigation.

metric_name.description:
The specific metric or condition that triggered the alert. Optional field populated when the alert is generated from a metric-based detection rule.

Examples: 'failed_login_count', 'api_error_rate', 'cpu_utilization', 'db_connection_pool_usage'. Null for alerts generated from audit log patterns or other non-metric sources.

metric_value.description:
The actual value of the metric that exceeded the threshold, triggering the alert. Stored as a string to accommodate various metric data types (numeric, percentage, text values).

Examples: '25', '12%', '85', 'HIGH'. Null when the alert was not triggered by a metric threshold breach.

threshold_value.description:
The threshold value that was exceeded by the metric, triggering the alert. The boundary condition that determined whether the alert should be generated.

Examples: '10', '5%', '80'. Stored as string for flexibility with different metric types. Null when not applicable to the alert type.

context_data.description:
Additional context or metadata related to the alert, stored in JSON format. Provides detailed information about the condition that triggered the alert.

Examples: IP addresses involved in failed login attempts, user IDs affected by unusual activity, system component names experiencing degradation, affected resource identifiers. The JSON structure varies by alert type to accommodate different contextual information needs.

todo_app_audit_log_id.description:
Optional reference to the audit log entry that triggered this alert. Foreign key referencing the `todo_app_audit_log.id` field.

Populated when the alert is generated from a specific audit event or activity pattern detected in audit logs. Null for alerts generated from system metrics or other monitoring mechanisms. Establishes traceability from alerts back to the specific events that triggered them.

oneOf.description: Open status. The alert is newly detected and has not yet been reviewed by an administrator. Open alerts require attention and investigation.
Acknowledged status. An administrator has reviewed the alert and is actively investigating the underlying condition. Signals that the alert is being handled.
Resolved status. The underlying condition has been addressed and the alert is closed. The incident is complete.

status.description:
The current state of the alert in its lifecycle. Tracks alert progression through the incident response workflow.

Possible values: 'open' (newly detected, unreviewed), 'acknowledged' (under investigation), 'resolved' (condition addressed, incident closed). Administrators update this field as they progress through alert investigation and response.

acknowledged_at.description:
Timestamp when an administrator acknowledged the alert, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Records the moment the alert was first reviewed and marked as acknowledged.

Null until the alert is transitioned to 'acknowledged' status. Provides audit trail information showing when incident response began.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when the alert condition was resolved or the alert was closed, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Records when the underlying issue was addressed.

Null until the alert is transitioned to 'resolved' status. Provides audit trail information showing when the incident was completed, enabling analysis of response times and incident resolution patterns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the alert was generated and created in the system, recorded in UTC. Marks the moment the alert condition was first detected.

Used for chronological ordering and trending analysis of alerts. Combined with `acknowledged_at` and `resolved_at`, provides complete timeline information for incident tracking.

ITodoAppAlert.description:
System alerts tracking anomalies, threshold violations, and conditions requiring administrator attention.

Monitors system health and detects suspicious patterns such as high failure rates, unusual access patterns, resource utilization thresholds, and security-related anomalies. Each alert record documents the condition detected, its severity level, when it was triggered, and the underlying metrics or audit entries that prompted the alert.

Alerts are derived from audit logs and system monitoring and serve to notify administrators of issues requiring investigation or intervention. Alert records are retained for historical trend analysis and incident investigation, allowing administrators to correlate multiple alerts to identify systemic issues or attack patterns.

Alerts support severity levels (info, warning, critical) to help administrators prioritize investigation and response efforts. The alert system enables proactive system management by detecting problems early before they impact users.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.description:
System-wide configuration settings that govern application behavior and operational constraints.

This table stores all configurable parameters that administrators use to tune system behavior, including authentication timeouts, password policies, rate limits, data retention policies, and performance settings.

System administrators modify these settings to control how the application operates. All system components read these settings to determine behavior. Settings are updated infrequently (typically during deployment or exceptional circumstances), and changes apply system-wide to all users.

Each setting is identified by a unique configuration key and stores its current value along with metadata about the setting type and description for administrative documentation.

Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering system settings.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.IUpdate.description:
Update request for system-wide configuration settings.

Allows administrators to modify configuration values in the todo_app_system_setting table. The operation validates new values against the setting's type and constraints (min_value, max_value for numeric settings) before persisting changes.

Only settings with is_editable=true can be modified. Attempting to update non-editable settings results in validation failure.

The operation automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to reflect modification time. Changes take effect system-wide immediately for all subsequent operations and all users.

Security-sensitive: This endpoint modifies critical system configuration affecting all users and components. Access must be strictly limited to system administrators. Changes to rate limiting, authentication timeouts, or password policies have significant security and operational impact.

ITodoAppSystemHealth.description:
Comprehensive system health information for administrative monitoring.

Provides administrators with immediate visibility into system operational status and capacity. Returns the current state of database connectivity, API server operations, authentication system status, and data storage accessibility.

Includes real-time performance indicators such as average API response times, system error rates, active sessions count, and request queue length. Resource utilization metrics help administrators monitor capacity constraints: CPU usage percentage, memory usage percentage, disk storage usage percentage, and database connection pool utilization.

All metrics are measured against defined thresholds (green for healthy, yellow for warning, red for critical) to enable quick assessment of system status.

Designed for the system health monitoring dashboard. Administrators regularly access this endpoint to verify system stability, identify emerging issues, and make decisions about system maintenance or scaling.

Response times are minimal (< 500ms) as this endpoint is frequently accessed during administrative monitoring. Data is current to within approximately 60 seconds as system metrics are refreshed at regular intervals.

name.description: Name of the critical system component (e.g., 'database', 'api_server', 'authentication_system', 'data_storage'). Identifies which system service or resource this health indicator represents.

oneOf.description: Health status of this specific component. 'healthy' (green) indicates normal operation. 'warning' (yellow) indicates degradation or approaching thresholds. 'critical' (red) indicates failure or severe issues.

Health status of this specific component. 'healthy' (green) indicates normal operation. 'warning' (yellow) indicates degradation or approaching thresholds. 'critical' (red) indicates failure or severe issues.

status.description: Health status of this specific component. 'healthy' (green) indicates normal operation. 'warning' (yellow) indicates degradation or approaching thresholds. 'critical' (red) indicates failure or severe issues.

message.description: Human-readable status message providing context or details about the component's current state. For healthy components, may describe normal operation. For degraded or critical components, explains the issue and any recommended actions.

last_check.description: Timestamp when this component's health was last checked in ISO 8601 format. Helps administrators determine freshness of the status information.

ITodoAppSystemHealth.IComponent.description:
Individual critical system component health indicator.

Represents the operational status of a specific critical service or resource that the system depends on. Components include database connectivity, API server status, authentication system status, and data storage accessibility.

Each component has a status (healthy, warning, or critical) indicating its current operational state measured against defined thresholds. The accompanying message provides context about the component's condition and any required actions.

The last_check timestamp indicates when this component's health was most recently verified, helping administrators assess the freshness of the information.

average_response_time_ms.description: Average API response time in milliseconds over the monitoring interval. Measures system responsiveness from the user's perspective. Healthy systems typically maintain response times below 200ms for standard operations.

error_rate_percent.description: Percentage of requests that resulted in errors during the monitoring interval. Calculated as (error_responses / total_requests) * 100. Lower values indicate better reliability. Acceptable error rates depend on operational requirements but typically should be below 0.1% for production systems.

active_sessions.description: Current number of active user sessions connected to the system. Indicates current system load and user engagement. Used for capacity planning and identifying unusual activity patterns.

request_queue_length.description: Number of incoming requests currently waiting in the processing queue. High queue lengths indicate the system is approaching capacity and may start rejecting requests. A queue length of zero indicates all requests are being processed immediately.

ITodoAppSystemHealth.IPerformance.description:
Real-time performance metrics indicating system responsiveness and capacity.

Measures how well the system is performing under current load. Average response time indicates user-facing system responsiveness. Error rate reveals reliability issues. Active sessions and request queue length indicate current system load relative to capacity.

These metrics help administrators identify performance degradation, detect approaching capacity limits, and make decisions about scaling or optimization.

cpu_usage_percent.description: Current CPU utilization as a percentage of total available capacity. Measured at the system or process level depending on monitoring granularity. Values above 80% indicate high load and potential bottlenecks. Values consistently above 90% suggest need for scaling or optimization.

memory_usage_percent.description: Current memory (RAM) utilization as a percentage of total available memory. High memory usage can cause system slowdown due to swapping or garbage collection. Values above 85% indicate resource pressure. Values consistently above 95% suggest memory leaks or need for scaling.

disk_usage_percent.description: Current disk storage utilization as a percentage of total available disk space. Includes space used by database files, logs, and application data. Values above 85% indicate limited remaining capacity. Values above 95% leave insufficient space for normal operations and should trigger cleanup or expansion.

database_pool_utilization_percent.description: Current database connection pool utilization as a percentage of maximum available connections. High utilization indicates database operations are consuming most available connections, limiting system's ability to handle additional concurrent database requests. Values above 80% suggest connection pool exhaustion risk.

ITodoAppSystemHealth.IResources.description:
System resource utilization metrics.

Measures current consumption of critical system resources: CPU processing capacity, memory (RAM) availability, disk storage space, and database connection pool availability.

Each metric is expressed as a percentage of total available capacity to enable quick assessment against defined thresholds (green for healthy, yellow for warning, red for critical).

Helps administrators monitor capacity constraints and plan for scaling or resource optimization. High utilization in any resource can cause system slowdown, errors, or service degradation.

ITodoAppUserStatistics.description:
Comprehensive user statistics and engagement metrics for system-wide user analysis.

This type aggregates all user-related statistics needed for administrative monitoring and analytics, including user counts, registration trends, activity patterns, and engagement indicators. The statistics provide insights into user base characteristics, growth patterns, and engagement levels across the entire Todo application.

The type encompasses multiple categories of metrics: user volume metrics (total registered users, active users by time period), registration trends (new users per day/week/month), engagement metrics (session duration, activity patterns), and retention metrics (users returning after first week).

These metrics are computed from the todo_app_user table and related audit/activity data, representing system-wide summaries rather than individual user records. The statistics support capacity planning, feature adoption analysis, and user engagement monitoring activities performed by system administrators.

total_users.description: Total count of all registered user accounts in the system. Includes both active and inactive (soft-deleted) accounts. This represents the complete user base size since system inception.

active_users_7d.description: Count of users who have been active (logged in or made API requests) within the last 7 days. Indicates the size of the engaged user base in the recent period.

active_users_30d.description: Count of users who have been active (logged in or made API requests) within the last 30 days. Provides a longer-term engagement measure.

active_users_today.description: Count of users active specifically today (current calendar day). Helps identify daily engagement levels and peak usage patterns.

new_users_24h.description: Count of new user registrations in the last 24 hours. Tracks short-term registration rate and growth velocity.

new_users_7d.description: Count of new user registrations in the last 7 days. Indicates weekly user acquisition rate.

new_users_30d.description: Count of new user registrations in the last 30 days. Provides monthly user acquisition metrics for capacity planning.

registration_trend.description: Daily breakdown of user registrations over the last 30 days. Array contains one entry per day showing registration count for that date. Enables visualization of registration patterns and identification of growth trends or anomalies.

active_users_this_week.description: Count of unique users active during the current calendar week. Week is defined starting from Monday. Measures current week engagement.

active_users_this_month.description: Count of unique users active during the current calendar month. Provides current month engagement metric.

average_session_duration_minutes.description: Average length of user sessions in minutes. Computed across all active user sessions. Indicates user engagement depth and time spent in the application per session.

user_retention_week_percent.description: Percentage of users who returned to the system after their first week of registration. Represents week-over-week retention rate. Values range from 0 to 100.

avg_todos_per_active_user.description: Average number of todo items created by each active user. Computed across all users who have created at least one todo. Indicates feature adoption and usage intensity.

avg_todos_completed_per_active_user.description: Average number of completed todo items per active user. Computed across users with completed todos. Measures productivity engagement level.

peak_usage_hour.description: The hour of the day (0-23 in 24-hour format) with the highest user activity. Identifies when system experiences peak load and when users are most active.

peak_usage_day.description: The day of the week with highest user activity. Values: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Shows weekly usage patterns.

users_deleted_30d.description: Count of user accounts deleted (soft-deleted) in the last 30 days. Tracks account churn and deletion frequency for capacity management.

concurrent_users_peak.description: Peak number of concurrent active users simultaneously connected to the system. Represents maximum concurrent load the system experiences. Used for infrastructure capacity planning.

IRegistrationTrendDay.description:
Daily registration count for a specific date.

Represents user registrations aggregated at the daily level, showing how many new users registered on a particular date. Part of the registration trend analysis used to visualize registration patterns and growth trends over the 30-day historical period.

date.description: The calendar date for this trend entry. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Represents the day on which the registration count was recorded.

count.description: Number of new user registrations on this specific date. Shows daily registration volume and helps identify registration pattern peaks and valleys.

ITodoAppTodoStatistics.description:
Aggregate statistical metrics about todo items across the entire system.

This type provides comprehensive statistical analysis of all todo items in the system, computed directly from the todo_app_todo table. It includes volume metrics, completion analysis, temporal distribution patterns, and usage indicators that help administrators understand application usage patterns and system engagement.

The statistics encompass total todo counts, completion rates, distribution by status, and temporal trends showing creation and completion patterns. These metrics support system monitoring, capacity planning, feature adoption analysis, and user engagement assessment across the entire user base.

Statistics are computed from aggregate queries without exposing individual todo items or personally identifiable information. The data reflects system-wide summaries useful for dashboards, admin monitoring, and analytics reporting.

total_todos.description: Total count of all todo items created in the system. Includes both completed and incomplete todos across all users.

completed_todos.description: Count of todo items marked as completed. Represents todos with is_completed = true.

incomplete_todos.description: Count of todo items not yet marked as completed. Represents todos with is_completed = false.

completion_rate_percent.description: Overall system completion rate as a percentage. Calculated as (completed_todos / total_todos) * 100. Values range from 0 to 100. Indicates the percentage of created todos that have been marked complete.

average_todos_per_user.description: Average number of todo items per user across all users. Computed as total_todos divided by total number of users. Indicates typical todo list size and feature adoption intensity per user.

todos_created_today.description: Count of todo items created on the current day. Tracks daily creation volume and current engagement level.

todos_created_7d.description: Count of todo items created within the last 7 days. Indicates recent creation activity and short-term engagement.

todos_created_30d.description: Count of todo items created within the last 30 days. Provides longer-term creation activity metric.

creation_trend.description: Daily breakdown of todo creation counts over the last 30 days. Array contains one entry per day showing how many todos were created on that date. Enables visualization of creation patterns and identification of usage peaks.

completion_trend.description: Daily breakdown of todo completion counts over the last 30 days. Array contains one entry per day showing how many todos were marked complete on that date. Shows completion patterns and productivity trends over time.

most_active_creation_hour.description: The hour of the day (0-23 in 24-hour format) with the highest todo creation activity. Identifies peak todo creation times in user workflows.

most_active_creation_day.description: The day of the week with highest todo creation activity. Values: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Shows weekly creation patterns.

todos_completed_today.description: Count of todos marked complete on the current day. Tracks daily completion activity.

todos_completed_7d.description: Count of todos marked complete within the last 7 days. Shows recent completion activity.

average_completion_time_days.description: Average number of days between todo creation and completion. Computed across all completed todos. Measures typical task completion timeline.

longest_incomplete_todo_days.description: Number of days since the oldest incomplete todo was created. Identifies longest-standing uncompleted task. Used to flag stale todos in user lists.

median_todos_per_user.description: Median number of todos per user. Provides statistical middle point that is less affected by outliers than average. Shows typical user behavior excluding power users and inactive accounts.

ITodoCreationTrendDay.description:
Daily todo creation count for a specific date.

Represents the number of todo items created on a particular date. Part of the creation trend analysis used to visualize patterns of todo creation activity over the 30-day historical period and identify peak creation times.

date.description: The calendar date for this trend entry. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Represents the day on which the creation count was recorded.

count.description: Number of todo items created on this specific date. Shows daily creation volume and helps identify activity patterns.

ITodoCompletionTrendDay.description:
Daily todo completion count for a specific date.

Represents the number of todo items marked as completed on a particular date. Part of the completion trend analysis used to visualize patterns of task completion activity over the 30-day historical period and understand productivity trends.

date.description: The calendar date for this trend entry. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Represents the day on which the completion count was recorded.

count.description: Number of todo items marked complete on this specific date. Shows daily completion volume and productivity patterns.

ITodoAppEngagementStatistics.description:
Aggregated engagement metrics about user and admin accounts in the system.

This schema represents comprehensive statistical data about user registration trends, activity patterns, and account status distribution. It combines metrics from both regular user and admin accounts to provide system-wide engagement insights.

The statistics include account creation trends, active user counts, admin counts, last activity timestamps, and soft-deletion tracking. These metrics are used by administrators and system operators to monitor platform health, track user growth, identify engagement trends, and make data-driven decisions about feature adoption and user retention strategies.

Soft-deleted accounts (where deleted_at is set) are excluded from active counts but tracked separately for compliance and audit purposes. The metrics provide insights into both current account status and historical engagement patterns.

total_users_count.description: Total number of active (non-deleted) regular user accounts in the system. Excludes users marked for soft deletion (deleted_at is not null). Used to track total active user base.

total_admins_count.description: Total number of active (non-deleted) admin accounts in the system. Excludes admins marked for soft deletion (deleted_at is not null). Used to track total active admin base.

deleted_users_count.description: Total number of users marked for soft deletion (deleted_at is not null). These accounts are retained for compliance and audit trail purposes but are not considered active.

deleted_admins_count.description: Total number of admins marked for soft deletion (deleted_at is not null). These accounts are retained for audit trail and compliance purposes but are not considered active.

users_created_today.description: Number of new user accounts created in the current day (UTC). Provides insight into user registration velocity and daily sign-up trends.

users_created_this_week.description: Number of new user accounts created in the current calendar week (UTC). Helps track weekly registration trends and seasonal patterns.

users_created_this_month.description: Number of new user accounts created in the current calendar month (UTC). Used for monthly cohort analysis and growth tracking.

admins_created_today.description: Number of new admin accounts created in the current day (UTC). Tracks admin account provisioning activity.

admins_created_this_week.description: Number of new admin accounts created in the current calendar week (UTC). Monitors admin account creation patterns.

admins_created_this_month.description: Number of new admin accounts created in the current calendar month (UTC). Tracks monthly admin account provisioning.

users_active_today.description: Number of user accounts with activity (API request or login) in the current day (UTC). Based on last_active_at timestamp. Indicates daily active user count.

users_active_this_week.description: Number of user accounts with activity in the current calendar week (UTC). Based on last_active_at timestamp. Measures weekly active user engagement.

users_active_this_month.description: Number of user accounts with activity in the current calendar month (UTC). Based on last_active_at timestamp. Key metric for monthly active user (MAU) tracking.

admins_active_today.description: Number of admin accounts with activity (API request or login) in the current day (UTC). Based on last_active_at timestamp.

admins_active_this_week.description: Number of admin accounts with activity in the current calendar week (UTC). Based on last_active_at timestamp.

admins_active_this_month.description: Number of admin accounts with activity in the current calendar month (UTC). Based on last_active_at timestamp.

average_days_since_user_activity.description: Average number of days since last_active_at for all active users. Decimal value. Indicates typical user engagement recency. Lower values indicate more frequent engagement.

average_days_since_admin_activity.description: Average number of days since last_active_at for all active admins. Decimal value. Monitors admin platform usage patterns.

user_retention_rate_30_days.description: Percentage of users who had activity (last_active_at) within the past 30 days relative to total users. Value between 0-100. Indicates 30-day user retention and engagement.

admin_retention_rate_30_days.description: Percentage of admins who had activity within the past 30 days relative to total admins. Value between 0-100. Monitors admin engagement over 30-day window.

account_creation_acceleration_ratio.description: Ratio comparing this month's user registrations to last month's user registrations. Value > 1.0 indicates accelerating growth, < 1.0 indicates slowing growth, = 1.0 indicates flat growth. Helps identify growth trends and inflection points.

user_churn_rate.description: Percentage of users who were active in previous month but inactive in current month. Value between 0-100. Indicates user loss rate and churn trends.

statistics_computed_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when these statistics were computed. Indicates data freshness and when the metrics were last calculated. Useful for understanding reporting latency.

data_period_start.description: Start timestamp (UTC) of the period covered by these statistics. Typically the beginning of the current calendar month or the earliest data point available. Used to understand the time window of the metrics.

data_period_end.description: End timestamp (UTC) of the period covered by these statistics. Typically the current timestamp when the report was generated. Marks the latest data point included in the metrics.
